title: Zephyrine and the Bakery
premise: Mirabel Delacroix has spent ten years rebuilding a quiet life around her bookshop and her daughter, hiding behind an anonymous correspondence that once kept her sane. When Zephyrine Okafor—the letter-writer she never met, now a baker—takes the lease next door, their written intimacy collides with a face-to-face reality neither expected. As the bakery's lease deadline forces Zephyrine toward a lucrative contract in another city, and Mirabel's old career offer resurfaces as the only way to save the bookshop, both must decide whether survival is worth another decade of invisibility. In the end, they choose each other publicly: Mirabel declines the job to co-sign the bakery lease, turning two fragile businesses into one shared doorway.
about_author: I. M. Galloway is the pen name of a former small-town bookseller who swears every romance begins in the aisle marked 'Local Interest.' They write love stories about people who are tired of being brave alone.

chapters.title: The Return Address That Wasn't
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Ten years of unsigned letters arrive at the bookshop on the anniversary of her husband's death, and for the first time one includes a forwarding address: the empty storefront next door. She burns the address rather than answer. Emotional beat: grief dressed up as routine, and the terror of being known.

chapters.title: Flour on the Doorstep
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Zephyrine moves in, opens the bakery, and recognizes Mirabel instantly from the letters' confessions—though Mirabel doesn't know who she is. Zephyrine chooses silence, delivering bread instead of revelations. Emotional beat: the delicious agony of intimacy without acknowledgment.

chapters.title: Marginalia
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. A customer returns a donated book with handwritten notes in the margins—notes that match the letters' voice exactly. Mirabel tests Zephyrine with a quoted line; Zephyrine deflects beautifully. Meanwhile Mirabel's daughter befriends the baker. Emotional beat: suspicion blooming into hope.

chapters.title: Closing Time Confessions
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. During a blackout, trapped together by a storm, Zephyrine nearly confesses by candlelight but stops when Mirabel describes the letter-writer as 'the only person who never asked me to be anything.' The lie of omission curdles. Emotional beat: closeness sharpened by guilt.

chapters.title: The Lease Clause
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. The landlord reveals the bakery lease expires in ninety days unless Zephyrine accepts a corporate contract out of state—a deal her estranged family brokered. She signs nothing, but tells no one, including Mirabel. Emotional beat: the price of survival counted in secrets.

chapters.title: What the Letters Never Said
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Mirabel finds Zephyrine's draft letters in a moving box while returning a borrowed tin—and learns the truth: the writer was the hospital volunteer from the worst year of her life. She flees without a word, feeling surveilled rather than loved. Emotional beat: betrayal reframe—tenderness experienced as exposure.

chapters.title: Ninety Days, Sixty Left
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Cold war next door: shut doors, returned bread, a daughter caught unhappily in between. Zephyrine decides to take the contract; Mirabel receives a job offer that would save the bookshop—at the cost of leaving town. Both choose flight. Emotional beat: parallel retreats, mirrored wounds.

chapters.title: The Reading
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. At the bookshop's monthly reading night, Mirabel reads an old letter aloud anonymously, telling the room what those words meant to a drowning woman. Zephyrine, in the back row, realizes Mirabel knew all along and came anyway. Emotional beat: public vulnerability as the first honest conversation.

chapters.title: Signature Required
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Climax. On the lease deadline, Zephyrine stands before the contract and the departure bus schedule. Mirabel arrives with her own refusal letter—declining the job—and offers to co-sign the bakery lease with her savings. They argue, weep, and finally say everything the letters couldn't. Emotional beat: choosing each other over safety, out loud.

chapters.title: One Doorway, Two Names
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV, epilogue-style. Spring: a connecting door is cut between bookshop and bakery; the daughter does homework among flour and fiction; a new anonymous letter arrives—this time signed, playful, addressed to both of them. Emotional beat: belonging chosen daily, invisibility gladly surrendered.
